growth_signal.value: Raised a $50M Series A in 2026 (about €43M), a big jump from its $8.75M round in 2024, with backers including RRE, Creandum, Coinbase Ventures and Franklin Templeton.

raised.value: $50M Series A (2026), after an earlier $8.75M round in 2024

entry.idea: Buying and trading things like stocks, bonds or funds is normally split across many separate, hard-to-connect systems, so Midas builds infrastructure that turns those investments into digital tokens so they can move and trade more easily online.
entry.lesson: When a new way of doing something (tokenising assets) starts to catch on, there is often more money in selling the infrastructure everyone needs than in selling directly to end users.
entry.name: Midas

growth.reason: Its funding jumped from $8.75M in 2024 to a $50M round in 2026, with well-known crypto and traditional-finance investors joining, though no user or revenue numbers are public.

market.reason: Tokenised investing could eventually touch a large part of global financial markets, though today it is still a specialised, early-stage niche.

tech.reason: Building compliant tokenisation infrastructure takes real engineering and regulatory work, but several other firms are building similar tokenisation platforms.

entry.twist: Instead of building another app for regular people to invest with, Midas builds the behind-the-scenes plumbing (tokenised investment infrastructure) that other financial companies plug into.
entry.who_pays: Banks, brokers and asset managers pay to use Midas's infrastructure to tokenise and distribute investment products to their own customers.
entry.why_now: Turning real financial assets into digital tokens ('tokenisation') is moving from a niche idea to something big banks and asset managers are testing, so infrastructure that makes this easy is in high demand.
